rawFindings.title: XSS vulnerability by unsanitized HTML content in TOC helper
rawFindings.explanation: The change replaced the text extraction and escaping using _.escape($(this).text()) with unsanitized HTML content using $(this).html(). This causes potential XSS vulnerabilities if the heading contains user-controlled HTML, because the HTML of the heading is directly injected into the TOC without escaping.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the previous safe escaping mechanism by using _.escape($(this).text()) instead of $(this).html() to ensure special HTML characters are properly escaped before inserting into the TOC output.

rawFindings.title: TOC helper may produce unescaped HTML leading to potential injection
rawFindings.explanation: The line `var text = $(this).html();` retrieves the inner HTML of the heading element instead of escaping the text content. This change allows raw HTML inside headings to be included unescaped in the TOC, potentially leading to injection of malicious code.
rawFindings.suggestion: Change the line back to `var text = _.escape($(this).text());` to ensure the text is properly escaped in the Table of Contents.

rawFindings.title: Potential XSS vulnerability by using raw HTML from headings in TOC helper
rawFindings.explanation: The change replaces escaping text content with raw HTML from headings in the Table of Contents helper. Previously, heading text was escaped to prevent injection of HTML or scripts. Now, the raw HTML of the heading is used directly, which may include untrusted HTML or scripts leading to cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities if the input is not controlled.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore escaping of heading text by using _.escape($(this).text()) instead of $(this).html() to prevent injection of malicious HTML or scripts.
